title: Processor-Subprocessor Risk Framework and Subprocessor Agreement Template
content:
Purpose: This is a working template to standardize how Redwood assesses, contracts with, and governs subprocessors (third-party processors) that will process customer data on behalf of Redwood. Intended to be used as an annex to the main Data Processing Agreement (DPA) or as a standalone Subprocessor Agreement where required.

High-level goals (non-exhaustive):
- Reduce legal review time for common subprocessors by providing a pre-approved control baseline.
- Capture minimal technical and contractual guardrails for private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and hosted services.
- Provide an operational onboarding checklist and renewal cadence for subprocessors.

Status: Draft - needs legal review and product sign-off for private-deploy specifics.

Quick notes / open questions (TODOs):
- Where do we set the threshold for 'high-risk' subprocessors vs 'standard'? propose: access to raw plaintext customer PII or ability to exfiltrate model weights -> high-risk. open to discussion. (owner: Maya)
- Insurance language: coordinate with finance to pin to current carrier limits (Jin).
- Private deployments: add optional clause for customer-managed KMS when subprocessor needs access to encrypted backups - product to confirm feasibility (SRE).

Definitions (short):
- Processor: Redwood Inference acting under the customer's DPA.
- Subprocessor: third-party engaged by Redwood to process customer data.
- Customer Data: as defined in the base DPA.
- High-risk processing: processing that includes access to unredacted PII, ability to train or alter models with customer data, or movement of data outside approved regions.

Template Sections (suggested ordering)
1) Scope and Purpose- The subprocessor shall process Customer Data only to provide the agreed services to Redwood and in accordance with documented instructions.
- Subprocessor must not use customer data for any other purpose (no repurposing for model training, analytics, etc.) unless explicitly authorized in writing.

2) Security Controls (baseline)- Logical access controls: role-based access with MFA for privileged accounts; monthly access reviews.
- Encryption: data at rest encrypted with industry-standard AES-256; data in transit TLS 1.2+ with strong ciphers.
- Key management: if Redwood keys are used, subprocessor must not persist plaintext keys; for customer-managed KMS specify allowed patterns.
- Vulnerability management: quarterly vulnerability scans and annual penetration test results shared under NDA.
- Logging and monitoring: retain access logs for at least 90 days; provide timelines for log access in incident investigations.

3) Data Location and Transfers- Subprocessor must process and store data only in permitted regions unless explicit written consent from Redwood and the customer.
- If cross-border transfer is necessary, subprocessor must ensure lawful transfer mechanisms (SCCs, adequacy, or other lawful basis).

4) Sub-subprocessors- Subprocessor may not engage sub-subprocessors without prior written consent from Redwood.
- Approval process: Redwood will review proposed sub-subprocessors via the onboarding checklist; automatic approval if meet pre-approved baseline (see Appendix A).

5) Audit, Certification, and Evidence- Redwood reserves the right to audit (onsite or remote) or request third-party audit reports (SOC2 Type II or equivalent).
- For high-risk subprocessors, require annual SOC2 Type II and an independent penetration test report.

6) Incident Notification and Response- Notification: subprocessor must notify Redwood within 24 hours of discovery of an incident impacting Customer Data.
- Containment and remediation plan: provide initial remediation plan within 72 hours; regular updates until resolved.
- Customer notification: Redwood will coordinate customer notification; subprocessor must cooperate fully.

7) Data Return and Deletion- Upon termination, subprocessor must securely delete or return Customer Data within 30 days, unless retention legally required.
- Provide certification of deletion when requested.

8) Liability and Indemnity- Maintain adequate insurance coverage; limits and specific line items TBD with Finance.
- Indemnify Redwood for breaches resulting from subprocessor negligence or willful misconduct.

9) Flow-down Obligations- All obligations in the base DPA that are applicable to processors must be flowed down to subprocessors handling Customer Data.

10) Specifics for Private Deployments- When the subprocessor needs connectivity to customer-managed infrastructure (e.g., private VPC peering, VPN):
  - Require least-privilege network access.
  - SSH and admin access must be via jump hosts with session recording.
  - No persistent backups outside customer-managed storage unless explicitly permitted.
  - If subprocessor requires access to model weights or cache, record purpose, duration, and required approvals.

Appendix A - Pre-approved control baseline (for fast-track approval)- Must have current SOC2 Type II or ISO 27001 certificate.
- Encryption in transit and at rest.
- Formal vulnerability disclosure program and remediation SLA.
- Documented access control policy and monthly reviews.

Appendix B - Onboarding checklist (operational)
- Legal: executed subprocessor agreement + insurance certificate.
- Security: share SOC2 report, latest pentest exec summary, architecture diagram showing where Customer Data flows.
- Product/Infra: network diagram for private deployments; list of required ports/peering.
- Ops: contact list, escalation path, maintenance windows.

Approval workflow (proposal)
- Triage: Security intake team (security-and-compliance) performs initial risk categorization using checklist. (JIRA-SEC-4821)
- Fast-track: if subprocessor meets Appendix A baseline and no private deployment access required -> auto-approve after security review.
- Full review: if high-risk or private deployment access requested -> security + legal + product review; approval requires sign-off from all three.

Record keeping and periodic review- Maintain a register of subprocessors, renewal dates, and last assessment.
- Annual reassessment for all active subprocessors; high-risk more frequent (recommended: 6 months).

Example Contract Clause (language to include in the Subprocessor Agreement Annex):
"Subprocessor shall process Customer Data only on documented instructions from Redwood and shall implement and maintain the security measures described in Appendix A. Subprocessor shall not retain, use or disclose Customer Data except as necessary to perform the services or as required by law. Subprocessor shall notify Redwood within 24 hours of becoming aware of any security incident affecting Customer Data and shall cooperate in incident response and remediation. Subprocessor agrees to flow down pertinent data protection obligations to any sub-subprocessor and shall remain liable for the acts and omissions of each sub-subprocessor."

Suggested rollout notes for internal teams (practical)
- Legal: use this template as a starting annex for most SaaS vendors; redact or strengthen private-deploy clauses as needed.
- Security: keep a short pre-approval checklist for vendors that are used frequently (CDN, monitoring, payments).
- Sales/Customer Success: if a customer asks for subprocessor list, direct them to the living register and point them to standard redaction policy.

Links / references (internal):
- Processor onboarding Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Processor+Onboarding+Checklist
- DPA master template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/LEGAL/DPA+Master+Template
- Prior vendor exceptions: JIRA-VEN-210, JIRA-VEN-317

Notes to reviewers (Maya):
- Check private-deploy specifics with Jin and SRE before finalizing.
- Confirm whether certification thresholds (SOC2 vs ISO) are acceptable for APAC customers.
- If we want automated approvals, product will need a small UI in Console to record approvals and store documents - file a tracker ticket.

Change log (brief):
- 2024-10-21: initial draft (Maya)
- 2024-11-12: added private-deployment checklist items (Sofia)
- 2024-12-05: added approval workflow draft (Liam)
- 2025-01-12: updated incident notification SLA and tags (Maya)

End of draft.

(If this template is useful, next steps: legal review, product feasibility for private-deploy clauses, then port approved language into the DPA annex generator in the contracts repo.)
